Finding 1: IntelPlayerState.pending is now one PendingSighting | null holding a set of types (PendingSightingType); a carrier-sighting body is { kind, tick, seenTick, sightings: [{ type, reason, sector, name }] } with one entry per type from the same older snapshot. step.ts: capped or data-less free triggers join the set (defer); at each boundary, and when an uncapped free trigger fires, flushPending replans every pending type: journal rumor, no-lead, or together in one sighting message; types without a readable snapshot entry stay pending. The cap is one sighting message per player per snapshot. Existing scripted tests were adapted only to the new body/pending shape (same scenarios and values). New scripted tests (alpha preset on the test sea): two pending types delivered together at the next boundary; a third trigger joins the set and all three go out in one message. The property checker now asserts after every step that each player has at most one pending message with unique types, and that each deferred type is delivered at the first boundary after it was capped, or else the checker proves it ineligible (dropped) or unreadable in the previous snapshot (still pending). EXERCISED adds sighting:deferred-delivered and sighting:several-types. Finding 2: the checker verifies every rumor: a cache target only when no sealed source of that type exists outside the recipient's active journal, and a carrier sighting only when no source or cache of the type exists. A new scripted test over 24 seeds, where a source and a cache are both eligible, checks that start, targeted and fresh rumors always pick a source. Mutation checks (run by hand, then reverted): delivering only the first pending type fails both new scripted tests and the alpha property run; letting caches compete with sources fails both scripted preference tests and two property runs. docs/intel.md now describes the settled rule. open_assumptions: The per-entry reason in a sighting message records which free trigger (start/fresh/replacement/targeted) asked for that type. The message has no top-level reason, since a merged message can mix triggers.

When an uncapped free trigger fires between boundaries, the pending message is flushed then too, so it goes out together with the new type rather than waiting. Within the same snapshot this can only add data, never an extra message, because the older snapshot does not change.

A pending type whose previous snapshot shows no other carrier stays pending for the following boundary (unchanged from intel-core-001). The checker allows this case and verifies it against the recorded snapshot.

findings.message: The bug the fix was meant to remove (a second sighting arriving up to a whole interval late) still happens when two sightings are triggered on the same tick and the player has not yet used this snapshot's sighting. In packages/simulation/src/intel/step.ts, freeLead (lines 382-392) is called once per type: 'for (const type of lost) freeLead(player, [type], "fresh")' (line 417) and 'for (const type of emptied) freeLead(player, [type], "replacement")' (line 434). The first uncapped call defers the type and immediately calls flushPending, which sends a one-type message and sets lastSightingBoundary. The next type on the same tick is then capped and waits for the next boundary. Examples: two thefts in one batched view (skipped ticks are a design requirement); a theft of sun on the same tick that A's moon rumor goes stale while every copy of both is carried; two journal rumors emptied on one tick. In each case the player gets one type now and the other up to 30 s later. The flush at a boundary (line 415) also runs before that tick's losses and replacements (lines 417 and 434), so a trigger on the boundary tick itself misses the message going out on that tick and waits a further interval. This goes against decisions.md ('A player who lost two types learns about both at the next boundary, not one interval apart'). It also makes docs/intel.md wrong where it says 'two types that need a sighting at once are delivered together at the next boundary, not one interval apart' and 'a player who lost two types learns about both at once'. The property checker (property.test.ts checkPending) cannot catch this: it only requires delivery at the first boundary after the type was capped, and the second type is capped by the first type's message on the same tick. Suggested fix: collect every free carrier trigger of a player's step, including the boundary flush, into the pending set, then flush once. Add a scripted test for two uncapped losses (or a loss plus a replacement) on one tick.

The scripted test 'prefer a sealed source, then a cache, then a carrier sighting' (intel.test.ts) asserts this. features/intel-core/intel-task.md, which the task says still applies, says a carrier sighting 'is sent only on three triggers: a fresh rumor after a loss when every other copy is carried, a targeted rumor under the same condition, or a journal replacement when every remaining copy is carried'. This is inherited from the restored snapshot, but it is a spec deviation that is neither documented as a decision nor covered by EXERCISED, which lists only sighting:fresh, sighting:targeted and sighting:replacement.

# Decisions: intel-core-fixes

From the overnight session of 2026-09-24/25. The operator is asleep and asked the assistant to decide, record each decision, and use the workflow for the code.

## Decisions

- intel-core-001 passed every check. The coverage reviewer blocked it on a real bug in deferred sightings, and the general reviewer was stopped before a verdict. This follow-up starts from the run's base (`9904848`, branch `intel/fixes-base`) and restores its snapshot (`9c1861e`), so the new reviewers see the whole feature plus the fixes.
- A carrier-sighting message may list several types. The cap is one message per player per snapshot, and a player has at most one pending message, holding a set of types. A player who lost two types learns about both at the next boundary, not one interval apart, and still gets no more than one sighting message per 30 s before minute 28 (still no tracker).
- The source-then-cache-then-carrier preference is proven by a property check on every rumor, not by one seed.

## Assumptions

- Everything else in `features/intel-core/` stands.

## Deferred

- Wiring and the journal UI: `objectives-endgame`.

concerns.message: The rule says a pending message is delivered at the next boundary "with every pending type that is still eligible", but never defines "eligible". This clashes with Finding 2's new property: "a carrier sighting only when no eligible source or cache existed at that tick". Suppose a type was deferred while every copy was carried, and before the boundary a cache of that type appears (disconnect expiry or quit, which the property runs generate). Delivering a sighting then fails the Finding 2 property. Dropping the type leaves a player who lost a rubbing with no lead at all, which breaks §11's free fresh rumor on loss. Recommended reading: a type stays eligible while the player still lacks it. At the boundary, run the normal lead generation again for each pending type, preferring sources, then caches, then carriers. A source or cache result becomes an ordinary journal rumor, which does not use the sighting cap. Carrier results go into the single sighting message. Drop a type only when the player now holds it, or when the older snapshot has no entry of that type held by someone else.
concerns.consequence: If the worker drops the type or still sends a sighting in this case, either the new Finding 2 property fails on a caching seed, or the player silently gets no lead for a loss. The latter is the same kind of deferred-delivery bug the coverage reviewer blocked intel-core-001 on, so this run could be blocked again.

concerns.message: The fix and its tests only cover types added while a player is already capped. When a player is not capped, two free triggers can arrive in the same step: a theft plus a journal rumor going stale on the same tick, or triggers batched by a skipped-tick step. The obvious implementation handles them one by one. It sends the first as a message, which uses up the cap, and defers the second to the next boundary. The settled rule allows one message with several types, so triggers from the same step should be combined into that one message.
concerns.consequence: In the uncapped same-step case, the second type still arrives a whole interval late. No named test catches this, so a reviewer will likely find it as the same bug in a new place. Add a scripted test: two sighting triggers in one step while uncapped produce one message listing both types.

concerns.message: The restore check `git diff --stat <ref> -- . ':!features'` prints nothing by construction after `git restore --source=<ref>`. It only proves the restore ran. It does not prove the snapshot changed only owned paths, which is what the first Stop condition needs checked.
concerns.consequence: If snapshot 9c1861e differs from the worker's base outside the owned paths (for example package-lock.json, tests/, a barrel file, or other work merged into the base since), the worker gets no signal. It could then ship changes outside its owned paths that other features own, and they would only surface as merge conflicts at integration. Also run `git diff --name-only HEAD -- . ':!features'` after the restore and check that every path is under an owned path.

concerns.message: Two of the new properties can pass by construction. First, the Finding 2 property only means something if the checker works out source and cache eligibility on its own from the world view: sealed source, island not claimed out, type the player lacks, not the stale target being replaced. It must not call the module's own candidate function. Second, "at most one pending message per player" is always true once pending is stored as one set per player. The real property is the delivery timing, measured from the step where the trigger was capped to the first step that crosses a boundary (a boundary counts once a step's tick reaches it, since ticks can be skipped).
concerns.consequence: A checker that reuses the implementation's eligibility logic would prove nothing, and the coverage reviewer, who already rejected a sampled check here, can block again on a tautological one.

concerns.message: Several choices are unspecified. The pending set and a multi-type message need a canonical order, and random-generator draws per type need a fixed order: use the preset's type order, not insertion order. Otherwise hashState, replays and sector picks depend on the order triggers happened to be processed in. Separately, in compressed test configs the minute-28 reveal may not fall on a carrier boundary. A type capped just before minute 28 would then wait for the next carrier boundary, while a trigger after minute 28 is sent at once. The checker's "first boundary after it was capped" has to match whichever behaviour is implemented.
concerns.consequence: The property runs may fail or be flaky on compressed seeds, or the replay test may give different hashState values across skipped-tick runs. That would use up verification attempts on test mismatches, not real bugs.

challenge.simpler_alternative: Treat pending as a per-player set of owed types, stored in the preset's type order, with one delivery path. Whenever sightings are due (right after triggers when the player is not capped, or at a carrier boundary when they are), run the normal free-lead generation for each owed type the player still lacks, in type order. Source or cache results become ordinary journal rumors. All carrier results go into the one sighting message for that snapshot. The same path handles triggers that arrive in the same step, deferred delivery, and Finding 2's preference rule. There is no second eligibility rule for the checker to mirror, and the \"one pending message\" invariant holds by construction.
challenge.cheap_experiment: In the worker's worktree, before any code changes, run three commands. First, `git cat-file -t refs/workflow/543db658493b6c2f/intel` to confirm the snapshot ref resolves from this worktree; its gitdir is ~/dev/project-B/.git, while the README names ~/dev/project-B-intel. Second, `git diff --name-only HEAD refs/workflow/543db658493b6c2f/intel -- . ':!features'` to confirm every changed path is under an owned path. Third, `git show refs/workflow/543db658493b6c2f/intel:packages/simulation/src/intel/step.ts | sed -n 330,390p` to see whether the current boundary delivery runs the source/cache preference again or only checks a snapshot entry. That shows whether the cache-appears case becomes a rumor, is dropped, or is still sent as a sighting, and so whether the \"still eligible\" rule needs pinning down before the worker writes the Finding 2 property.

# Task: intel

## Goal

Deliver the `intel-core` feature (the pure rumors, journal, sectors and reveals) with its review findings fixed. Run intel-core-001 built it and passed every check. Its coverage reviewer blocked it on a real bug: a player with two deferred sightings got the second a whole interval late. Its general reviewer was stopped before a verdict. Start from that run's snapshot, fix the findings, and the whole feature is reviewed again.

## Context

- `features/intel-core/intel-task.md` and `features/intel-core/decisions.md` define the feature, and all of it still applies. Read them first.
- **First step:** restore intel-core-001's snapshot (commit `9c1861e`) into your worktree, deletions included, but not `features/`:
  `git restore --source=refs/workflow/543db658493b6c2f/intel --staged --worktree -- . ':!features'`.
  Check with `git diff --stat refs/workflow/543db658493b6c2f/intel -- . ':!features'` (it must print nothing). Then read `docs/intel.md`.
- The verifier runs `npm ci`, then `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:unit`, `npm run test:integration` and `npm run build`.
- Other features run at the same time and own the sea, server, web and tests, plus `packages/*/src/objectives`. Stay inside your owned paths.
- **This machine is shared by several runs. Never stop processes by name pattern (`pkill -f`, `killall`, and so on). Stop only the PIDs you started.**

## Findings to fix (coverage reviewer)

1. **(P1) Deferred sightings for several types.** `step.ts:344` queues one pending entry per type, and `step.ts:370-379` delivers the first at the boundary, which uses up that snapshot's sighting and puts the second back. So it arrives a whole interval late. **Settled rule:**
   - A carrier-sighting message may list several types (one entry per type, all from the same older snapshot).
   - The cap is **one sighting message per player per snapshot** before minute 28.
   - A player has at most **one pending** deferred message, which holds the **set** of pending types. A new capped free trigger adds its type to that set.
   - At the next boundary, the pending message is delivered with every pending type that is still eligible.
   - Update `docs/intel.md` to say so.
   - **Tests:**
     - scripted: two pending types are delivered together at the next boundary;
     - scripted: a third trigger joins the set;
     - property checker: after every step, each player has at most one pending message, and a deferred trigger is delivered at the first boundary after it was capped (or dropped only because its type became ineligible, which the checker verifies).
2. **(P2) Target preference proven, not sampled.** Sources before caches is checked on one seed at one step. Add a property check: whenever a rumor targets a cache sector, no eligible sealed source of that type existed at that tick; whenever it's a carrier sighting, no eligible source or cache existed. Add scripted cases over at least 20 seeds where both a source and a cache are eligible: every one picks the source.

## Constraints

- Owned paths as in `policy.json`. Apart from restoring the snapshot, change only what the findings need. Keep the structure, names and every existing test (adapt the one-type deferral test to the settled rule if its expectations change).

## Acceptance

- The restored `intel-core` feature meets all of `features/intel-core/intel-task.md`'s acceptance, with "one carrier sighting per player per snapshot" now meaning one sighting **message**.
- Findings 1–2 are fixed with the tests they name.
- `npm ci` then `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:unit`, `npm run test:integration` and `npm run build` pass from a clean checkout.

## Stop

Report `blocked` instead of continuing when any of these happens:

- Restoring the snapshot fails or touches a path outside the owned paths.
- `npm ci` or an install fails twice for reasons outside the repository (registry, network).
- A check can pass only by changing a path outside the owned paths.
- After ninety minutes of work, any required check still fails and you cannot name the next fix.

Report `question` only for a choice that would change this acceptance.

completion.summary: Restored intel-core-001's snapshot (9c1861e) excluding features/; git diff --stat against the snapshot printed nothing and every restored path is owned. Finding 1: IntelPlayerState.pending is now one PendingSighting | null holding a set of types (PendingSightingType); a carrier-sighting body is { kind, tick, seenTick, sightings: [{ type, reason, sector, name }] } with one entry per type from the same older snapshot. step.ts: capped or data-less free triggers join the set (defer); at each boundary, and when an uncapped free trigger fires, flushPending replans every pending type: journal rumor, no-lead, or together in one sighting message; types without a readable snapshot entry stay pending. The cap is one sighting message per player per snapshot. Existing scripted tests were adapted only to the new body/pending shape (same scenarios and values). New scripted tests (alpha preset on the test sea): two pending types delivered together at the next boundary; a third trigger joins the set and all three go out in one message. The property checker now asserts after every step that each player has at most one pending message with unique types, and that each deferred type is delivered at the first boundary after it was capped, or else the checker proves it ineligible (dropped) or unreadable in the previous snapshot (still pending). EXERCISED adds sighting:deferred-delivered and sighting:several-types. Finding 2: the checker verifies every rumor: a cache target only when no sealed source of that type exists outside the recipient's active journal, and a carrier sighting only when no source or cache of the type exists. A new scripted test over 24 seeds, where a source and a cache are both eligible, checks that start, targeted and fresh rumors always pick a source. Mutation checks (run by hand, then reverted): delivering only the first pending type fails both new scripted tests and the alpha property run; letting caches compete with sources fails both scripted preference tests and two property runs. docs/intel.md now describes the settled rule. Checks run: npm ci, npm run typecheck, npm run test:unit (572 passed), npm run test:integration (36 passed), npm run build (smoke passed), all exit 0. After that, a comment-only rewrap in step.ts; typecheck and the intel unit tests were rerun and pass.
open_assumptions: The per-entry reason in a sighting message records which free trigger (start/fresh/replacement/targeted) asked for that type. The message has no top-level reason, since a merged message can mix triggers.

When an uncapped free trigger fires between boundaries, the pending message is flushed then too, so it goes out together with the new type rather than waiting. Within the same snapshot this can only add data, never an extra message, because the older snapshot does not change.

A pending type whose previous snapshot shows no other carrier stays pending for the following boundary (unchanged from intel-core-001). The checker allows this case and verifies it against the recorded snapshot.
untested: Mixed reasons (fresh plus replacement) in one delivered sighting message are only reached in the property runs, not asserted by a scripted test.
The objectives-endgame wiring and the journal UI that render the new multi-entry carrier-sighting body don't exist yet.
